title: Exact recognition of bounded clique-width
formal: For every fixed integer \(k\ge 1\), do there exist a deterministic Turing machine \(A_{k}\) and constants \(C_{k},c_{k}\ge 1\) such that \(A_{k}\) decides whether \(\operatorname{cw}(G)\le k\) for every finite simple undirected graph G in at most \(C_{k}(N+1)^{c_{k}}\) steps, where N is the bit length of G’s adjacency-matrix encoding?
why: Tests whether a major dense-graph width parameter admits efficient exact recognition at every fixed value.

progress.text: The variable-threshold recognition problem is proved NP-complete; the paper explicitly leaves recognition at each fixed threshold open.
The full polynomial-time recognition algorithm for clique-width at most three is published.
New graph algorithms exploit a supplied clique expression; they do not determine whether such an expression exists at an exact threshold.

definitions: A k-expression is a finite expression building a labeled graph using labels from \(\{1,\ldots ,k\}\). It can create one isolated vertex with a chosen label; take the disjoint union of two previously constructed labeled graphs; add all edges between the vertices labeled i and those labeled j for distinct i,j; or change every label i to j. Edge insertion leaves existing edges in place without duplicating them. Relabeling changes no edges. The two operands of a disjoint union may both be arbitrary expressions, so this is ordinary clique-width, not linear clique-width. For a nonempty graph \(G, \operatorname{cw}(G)\) is the least k for which some k-expression produces a graph isomorphic to G after labels are erased. Set \(\operatorname{cw}(\varnothing )=0\). The input contains \(n\ge 0\) and the \(n\times n\) symmetric zero-diagonal \(0/1\) adjacency matrix for the graph on \(\{1,\ldots ,n\}\). It contains no construction expression or promise about its width. \(A_{k}\) outputs YES exactly when \(\operatorname{cw}(G)\le k\) and NO otherwise, always halting with the stated worst-case bit bound. The quantifier order is \(\forall k \exists A_{k},C_{k},c_{k} \forall G: k\) is fixed for each machine, and the polynomial exponent may depend on it. Each \(A_{k}\) is a single finite program with no advice depending on graph size; the statement imposes no effective map from k to its program and no uniform exponent.
answer_criterion: Prove polynomial-time exact recognition for every fixed threshold k in the model stated, or prove that for at least one fixed k the language \(\{G:\operatorname{cw}(G)\le k\}\) has no deterministic polynomial-time decider. An expression with more than k labels does not establish a YES answer; failure of one construction does not establish NO. Variable-k NP-hardness, or fixed-k hardness under an unproved assumption, does not alone unconditionally refute this proposition.

context_blocks.title: A width that permits dense graphs
context_blocks.text: Clique-width counts reusable labels in a construction, not the size of a largest clique. Every nonempty edgeless graph has width 1. Complete graphs with at least two vertices have width 2, regardless of their size. Thus even very dense graphs can have small clique-width; the parameter captures how uniformly groups of vertices can be assembled.

context_blocks.title: Fixed thresholds versus the general optimization problem
context_blocks.text: Fellows and coauthors prove NP-completeness when both G and k are input. The present statement allows a different polynomial bound for each fixed k. For example, a hypothetical bound \(N^{k+2}\) would be polynomial for each such threshold, while not giving a polynomial bound when k grows with N. The source lists fixed-threshold recognition separately from the stronger FPT question, which asks for one algorithm with runtime \(f(k)N^{c}\) and c independent of k.

context_blocks.title: Small thresholds are understood
context_blocks.text: Polynomial-time recognition is known through \(k=3\), with the full three-label algorithm published by Corneil and coauthors in 2012. The cited sources retain \(k=4\) as the first unresolved threshold. A solution only for four labels would still leave the card’s quantification over every fixed k.

context_blocks.title: Approximate or supplied decompositions serve a different purpose
context_blocks.text: A procedure that returns an expression with \(f(k)>k\) labels for graphs of width at most k can enable other graph algorithms, yet leave the exact threshold undecided. Likewise, the July 2026 feedback-vertex-set result assumes a k-expression is already supplied. These results explain the usefulness of clique-width without providing the recognizer requested here.

sentences: Clique-width measures how many reusable vertex labels are needed to build a graph with four specified operations.
Even a complete graph of arbitrary size needs only two labels.
The question asks whether graphs of width at most k can be recognized in polynomial time for every fixed k.
The polynomial exponent may depend on k, so known NP-completeness when k is input does not settle it.
Small thresholds are understood, while approximate or supplied decompositions do not give exact recognition at every threshold.
